about: Four photographs taken round Canada Water Library, SE16, and given to the project under CC0 by the owner. This file holds the hand-made part: what each photo shows, how each building was identified, and the facade regions to rectify. The measurements are made by the logged operation rectify-facade-patches and the graph by lift-contrib-photos (magpie/cwplans/tools/contrib-photos.mjs). Skills: docklands-data-curation ('Contributed photos'), photo-view-reconstruction.
creator: danbri (project owner)
time: about 16:30 BST (owner); the files carry no EXIF time, GPS or camera data
sun: 2026-10-06 15:30 UTC: azimuth 238.7 deg true, altitude 16.3 deg (astronomy-engine, tools/view-mcp sunAt)
osm_extract: Geofabrik greater-london-latest.osm.pbf of 2026-10-02 (magpie/cwplans/data/raw/docklands/), cut with osmium to -0.062,51.491,-0.036,51.505
model: magpie/cwplans/docklands/data/area.js built 2026-10-03; building index, top (m OD), base and height source at that build

ontario-point.name: Ontario Point
ontario-point.footprint: near-square, sides 24.2 m (bearing 27 deg) and 24.0 m (bearing 149 deg), from the OSM outline

faces_seen.south-west: main face in photo 1 (normal 239 deg: it faced the sun)
faces_seen.north-west: narrow face on the left in photo 1

facade.south_west_face: Symmetric, 24.0 m wide: corner pier | 3-pane bay | pier | pane | louvre | pane | pier | pane | louvre | pane | pier | pane | louvre | pane | pier | 3-pane bay | corner pier. 12 glazing panes, 3 dark vertical louvre strips (full height), 4 inner piers, 2 corner piers. Panes about 1.2 m, louvre pitch about 4.6 m (rectified patch ontario-point-sw-top, face width from OSM).
facade.vertical_module: A thick slab band every two floors and a thin transom halfway between: about 12 two-floor units above the ground floor. Floor about 3.06 m (model height 76.5 m / 25 levels).
facade.north_west_face: Glazed winter gardens (balconies closed by glass), one row a floor, on a dark frame.
facade.top: Open roof frame about one and a half floors tall: thin vertical fins on a top beam, over a glass balustrade (roof terrace). A tall thin fin rises at the west corner.
facade.base: Double-height ground floor, the name ONTARIO POINT in metal letters at the left of the south-west face.
facade.materials: Light warm-grey stone or precast piers and spandrels; blue-reflective glass; dark grey louvre strips.
facade.how: judged from photo 1 and the rectified patches; counts checked on the full-width patch

identified_by: the name ONTARIO POIN(T) on the building in photo 1
OSM way 204580680 has addr:housename Ontario Point and 25 levels
floor count: about 12 two-floor units plus the ground floor, about 25 levels; model LiDAR height 76.5 m
the chimney in the lower left (OSM way 1175339088) lies north-west of the tower, as for a camera south-west of it looking north-east, which is also the face that the sun lit

canada-water-library.name: Canada Water Library
canada-water-library.footprint: longest sides 42.0 m (bearing 73 deg) and 34.8 m (bearing 110 deg), from the OSM outline; the building widens upward (an inverted pyramid), so the footprint is smaller than the roof

facade.wall: Expanded-metal panels with a diamond mesh, warm grey-brown (bronze), in a staggered panel grid. The walls lean out: the building is wider at the top.
facade.windows: Tall framed windows that project from the wall as boxes, 2 panes across and 3 to 4 high, bronze frames; five on the north face in photo 2, at differing heights.
facade.base: Glazed ground floor with a black fascia and the words CANADA WATER LIBRARY in white capitals; a maroon double door with a leisure centre advertisement.
facade.how: judged from photo 2 and the rectified patch library-north-wall

identified_by: the words CANADA WATER LIBRARY on the building

canada-water-station.name: Canada Water station (Jubilee line ticket hall drum)

model.note: no outline of its own in the model; the nearest model blocks (guessed height 6 m) are 7.5 m away

facade.form: A glass drum (cylinder) about 30 m across (OSM outline: radius 13.7 to 16.8 m, perimeter 95.8 m) under a thin overhanging disc roof, dark grey; mullions and transoms in a regular grid.

identified_by: the glass drum with a disc roof next to the bus station canopy
OSM way 41599363 (building train_station, name Canada Water)

canada-water-bus-station.name: Canada Water bus station

facade.form: Low glazed canopy with a pitched translucent roof and a pointed end, left of the drum in photo 3.

identified_by: position: the canopy round the drum

columbia-point.name: Columbia Point

faces_seen.north-east: left tower in photo 3, backlit (judged: the camera was east of the drum)

facade.main_face: Cream concrete frame; a pair of windows in each bay between red-brown panels; a glazed column (stair or lift lobby) at the right; in the left bay a recessed balcony row every fourth floor.
facade.side_face: Projecting balconies with dark rails, stacked.
facade.top: Plant room box above the roof, set back.
facade.how: judged from photo 3 and the rectified patch columbia-point-face

identified_by: two identical towers of about 20 floors directly west of the drum: OSM ways 52588474 and 52588475 are the only towers of that height there, 71 m apart

the-founding.name: The Founding (Canada Water plot A1)

model.height_source: levels (the building is newer than the 2022 LiDAR)

the-founding.published: 35-storey residential tower by Allies and Morrison for British Land and AustralianSuper; 'a tripartite tower structure atop a five-storey podium' (https://www.gardiner.com/projects/plot-a1-canada-water)

faces_seen.east or north: photo 4, in shade (judged: camera north-east of the tower)

facade.parts: Two of the three tower parts are visible in photo 4: a part with a red (oxide-red) frame and projecting balconies on the left, and a taller dark charcoal part on the right with a grid of windows and a column of projecting balconies at its left edge; an open frame crown at the top.
facade.windows: Each floor of the dark part: two windows a bay, each with horizontal glazing bars, in a dark metal frame grid.
facade.how: judged from photo 4 and the rectified patch the-founding-dark-face; colours are in shade

identified_by: floor count: 27 floor rows in the rectified region (even 82 px spacing), with the top and the lowest floors outside it, so 30 or more floors
the only building within about 1 km with 30 or more levels in OSM is The Founding (35); the next is Ontario Point (25, fully glazed, photo 1)
published form: three tower parts on a podium; photo 4 shows two parts of different height and colour
